title: Stepped route grammar, validator, and rollback hooks
content:
Purpose:
This is a working layout for a rule grammar (JSON/YAML) + validator behavior + rollout/gating mechanics for stepped routing policies in the control plane. Objective is to capture a compact, machine-parseable schema and a set of deterministic validation rules so infra can reject unsafe changes and the rollout engine can perform safe progressive launches across regions and capacity tiers.

High-level goals (short):
- Define a concise rule object that supports priority, predicate composition, locale/region scope, model-variant affinity, and fallback chains.
- Provide validator checks that are deterministic and cheap (O(n) over rule clauses).
- Describe rollout recipe for canaries, regional rollouts, and automatic rollback triggers.
- Ensure observable signals (latency, error-rate, cost-per-token, quality-regression) are wired to gating.

Non-goals:
- Full policy language for user-defined scripting (we keep predicates declarative).
- Long-term storage format (this is authoring + gating contract).

Quick example (YAML-ish for readability):

# top-level rule set (array of rules evaluated in order of priority)
- id: route-2025-10-01-stepped-abr
  priority: 50              # lower number = higher precedence
  description: "Prefer cheaper quantized variant in EU except for low-latency customers"
  predicates:
    - all:
      - region_in: ["eu-west-1", "eu-central-1"]
      - customer_tier != "enterprise"
  actions:
    primary_variant: redwood-llama-q4-kv-8bit
    fallback_chain:
      - redwood-llama-q8
      - redwood-llama-fp16
    max_batch_ms: 8
    allow_streaming: true
    metrics_tag: "stepped-abr-q4"
  rollout:
    mode: stepped
    steps:
      - pct: 1
        duration_minutes: 20
      - pct: 10
        duration_minutes: 30
      - pct: 50
        duration_minutes: 60
  gating_signals:
    - name: p95_latency_ms
      threshold: 300
      direction: below
    - name: error_rate
      threshold: 0.005
      direction: below

Key schema fields (flattened description):
- id (string): stable authorable id, used for auditing and rollback commands.
- priority (int): evaluation order; collisions are allowed but documented.
- description (string): free text for owners.
- predicates (list): declarative clauses; supported operators: in, not_in, ==, !=, exists, not_exists, regex. Also boolean composition: any, all, not. No script functions.
- primary_variant (string): model variant name to route to when predicates match.
- fallback_chain (list[string]): ordered fallback variants. Must include at least one variant that is compatible (validated against model registry).
- max_batch_ms (int): upper bound to allow batching at the runtime; 0 disables batch.
- allow_streaming (bool): runtime hint.
- metrics_tag (string): optional tag to emit custom metrics for this rule.
- rollout (object as inline string in authoring UI): mode in {instant, stepped, region-first, canary-by-customer}. Steps array for stepped mode.
- gating_signals (list): each with name, threshold, direction (below/above), window_minutes, aggregation (p95/p50/avg).

Validator rules (must be implemented in control-plane authoring service):
1) Schema conformance: all required fields present and types correct.
2) Variant compatibility: primary_variant and all fallback entries must exist in model catalog and be marked compatible with request shape (embedding vs llm vs chat).
3) Priority conflicts: if two rules have identical priority and overlapping predicates, raise warning and require explicit tie-breaker (owner resolution or rule_group).
4) Deterministic predicate checks: predicates must be normalizable into canonical form for overlap detection (sort keys, expand singletons).
5) Rollout sanity: total pct in last step <= 100; steps are monotonically increasing pct; each step duration >= 5 minutes unless override flag set.
6) Gating signal validity: referenced metrics must exist for target model/route; thresholds must have a baseline reference (last 7 days median).
7) Multi-region safety: a rule that assigns different primary_variant across regions must include a cross-region fallback that can serve in both regions or a migration plan.
8) Ownership + contact: each rule must list owner and an oncall contact (email/Slack) for auto-rollbacks and incident escalation.

Validation outputs: validator should produce machine-readable problems as lines:
- ERROR: VARIANT_NOT_FOUND: redwood-llama-q4 (route-2025-10-01-stepped-abr)
- WARN: PRIORITY_OVERLAP: route-A & route-B (overlap pct 0.42)
- INFO: GATING_BASELINE_LOW_CONFIDENCE: p95_latency_ms baseline < 100 samples

Rollout mechanics (recommended flow):
- Authoring: user submits rule via console/infra API.
- Pre-check: synchronous validator run that rejects on ERROR and returns warnings.
- Dry simulation: run rule through traffic-sim with historical traffic trace (at least 1 hour sample) to produce expected route distribution and fallback activation rates. Show simulated cost delta and latency delta.
- Canaries/Stepped: for stepped mode we rely on control-plane token sampler that marks X% of requests deterministically using a hash(key) mod 100. This ensures consistent session stickiness during rollout steps.
- Monitoring: wire metrics for the route tag and aggregate by step bucket (canary-1, canary-10, etc).
- Automated gating: at the end of each step the gating engine checks configured signals over the step window + a stabilization buffer (default 2 minutes). If any signal is outside threshold, initiate automatic rollback to last safe step or full rollback.
- Rollback hooks: rollback should be a single API call that either retracts the rule or resets the rollout steps to previous state. Rollback triggers: high error spike, p95 regression > 2x baseline, SLI breach for more than N minutes.

Multi-region specifics:
- Rule scope: rules may be scoped to region_in, region_not_in, continent, or global.
- Primary constraint: cannot route to a variant that lacks deployment in the rule's region unless rule includes cross-region network routing (explicit allow_cross_region: true) and the variant passes cross-region latency tests.
- Region-first rollout: allow a rollout.mode = region-first where we fully convert a single region (100%) then expand to others. This is useful when model artifacts must be warm in-place.
- Drift detection: run periodic checks to compare per-region SLOs; if variant performs poorly in one region compared to another by >20% latency difference, mark the rule as degraded and optionally reduce traffic in that region.

Observability checklist for each rule:
- metrics: p50/p95 latency, error rate, server-side cost-per-token, prompt/response token counts, fallback activation rate, model-confidence (if available).
- traces: sampling at 1/100 requests with annotation of rule_id and step bucket.
- logs: authoring event, validator results, rollout step transitions, automated rollback events.
- audit: who changed rule and a human-readable diff attached to the rule record.

Operational playbook (short):
- Day 0: Author rule in UI, run dry-sim, schedule rollout window with owner.
- Day 1: Start stepped rollout at low-traffic hours; watch gating signals and payment/cost signals.
- If automated rollback triggers: owner receives page, rollback is performed automatically; investigation ticket created with pre-populated diagnostics (trace ids, sample requests).
- If warnings only: owner must acknowledge warnings before proceeding to next step.

Open questions / TODOs:
- How to represent complex customer-level targeting (percent by customer cohort) — do we extend rollout.mode or add separate customer-target policy?
- Exact canonicalization algorithm for predicates needs to be defined (we should reuse existing route-normalizer in control-plane repo).
- Should we allow user-defined custom metrics in gating_signals? Risk: metric availability and baseline quality.
- Backwards-compatibility: plan for migrating legacy routing YAMLs to this new schema; we may need a compatibility layer in the authoring API.

Notes to self / implementation hints:
- Keep validator idempotent and fast; aim for <150ms per rule check for typical rule size (<20 predicates).
- Use deterministic hashing for pct rollout bucket assignment; include salt derived from rule id to avoid accidental correlation between rules.
- When computing overlaps, use predicate bounding (region sets, known customer ids) to short-circuit expensive set intersections.

References and links: see linked_artifacts above and internal traces: #routing-engine-sim, infra/pr-189 for validator library.

Owner/approver: Aisha Patel (eng-platform) ; please ping Diego Ramos for rollout orchestration UX.

Last note: this document is a working draft; move to "in_review" after we land validator library and a first dry-run simulation in staging.
